newsitem.title: USA: New product designed to block poison ivy's effect.
newsitem.headline: New product designed to block poison ivy's effect.

text.p: For many outdoorspeople, summer is synonymous with poison ivy. Add to that poison oak and poison sumac.
There is an arsenal of products to help suffers after exposure to these plants, but a pharmaceutical company has develop ed a lotion that aims to offer protection before exposure.
IvyBlock skin protectant is a lotion from EnviroDerm Pharmaceuticals, of San Francisco, Calif., and is available nationwide.

"Until now there's been no viable pre-exposure poison ivy, oak and sumac barrier cream that works," said Dr. Joseph Fowler, a member of EnviroDerm's scientific advisory board and a dermatologist in Louisville, Ky.

IvyBlock lotion has received clearance from the Food and Drug Administration. It is applied as a lotion that dries quickly. It contains a formula that helps block skin contact with urushiol, the oil in the plants that triggers the rash.
Poison ivy can affect two out of three Americans, and the company said that of those, 15 percent may have severe allergic reactions that require medical treatment.
IvyBlock should be applied to skin at least 15 minutes before possible contact with poisonous plants and re-applied every four hours. The lotion coating can be removed with soap and water.
It comes in a four-ounce bottle and sells for about $12.
The company expects a complete roll-out by Memorial Day and the product should be available in drug stores, supermarkets and mass merchandisers.
Enviroderm has a web site. http://www.ivyblock.com.
Helena, Calif.-based Beringer Vinyards is offering Wine Tasting Wheels, devices designed to help wine drinkers identify, describe and remember aromas and flavors of red and white wines.
The Wheels are patterned after the original Wine Tasting Wheel created by Professor Ann. C. Noble of the University of California at Davis.

The Wheels feature terms commonly used to describe the aromas, tastes and flavors of the wines, and how they feel in the mouth. Common descriptive words are listed in connection with certain wines, such as pineapple and vanilla for Chardonnay; and black pepper and blackberry for Zinfandel.

To receive a Beringer Wine Tasting Wheel, send $3 to Beringer Vinyards' Fulfilment Centre, 615 Airpark Road, Napa, Calif. 94558. One dollar will be donated to the sensory research department at U.C. Davis and $2 goes for shipping and handling.
Bozart Toys, a Philadelphia-based company that makes non-violent, creative toys designed by museum quality visual artists, has introduced three new toys.

Marco the Magnificant, for children ages 18 months and up, is a musical Jack-in-the-box featuring Marco the rabbit. It was designed by Jon Kessler, whose sculptures have been exhibited at the Museum of Modern Art and the Whitney Museum in New York.
World On Wheels, also designed by Kessler, is a push-pull toy featuring a globe that chimes as it turns on a reflective chassis. It is aimed at children one year and older.
Dunstan the Dragon is an easy-to-use green dragon marionette designed by Daniel Oates, who has exhibited his sculpture worldwide.
All of the toys will cost about $25. For more information, call the company at 215-627-2223.
Kate Spade Handbags, making fashion statements in New York and other fashion capitals, has joined the Baby Boom.

The Kate Spade Baby Bag line is being introduced at upscale department stores including Saks and Barney's and Nieman Marcus, offering mothers a bag that can carry baby's necessities while doubling as a sophisticated carry-all.

The bags are designed with wipeable compartments, extra large zipper pockets, side or inner pockets for bottles and a soft, oversized changing pad. Other than what's inside, the bags are similar to the signature shapes in the current Kate Spade line.
The Baby Bags range in price from $95 to $250, including the changing pad. Replacement pads cost $30.
For more information, contact the Kate Spade store in New York at 212-965-0301.
